newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-NEW ENGLAND LEADS SUPER BOWL AFTER FIRST QUARTER.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-NEW ENGLAND LEADS SUPER BOWL AFTER FIRST QUARTER.

text.p: The New England Patriots led the heavily favoured Green Bay Packers 14-10 after the first quarter of Super Bowl XXXI on Sunday.
The Packers had the early momentum but New England turned it around behind the passing of quarterback Drew Bledsoe.
Bledsoe completed 8-of-15 for 123 yards and two touchdowns in the quarter.
The Packers struck fast, scoring a touchdown on their second offensive play of the game.
After forcing the Patriots to punt on their opening drive, Green Bay's Desmond Howard returned Tom Tupa's punt 32 yards to the Green Bay 45-yard-line.
Two plays later, Brett Favre completed a perfect 54-yard socring pass to Andre Rison, who had blown past defender Otis Smith. Rison high-stepped into the end zone for the touchdown.
On the second play of New England's next drive, Bledsoe was picked off by Green Bay cournerback Doug Evans, who stepped in front of the intended receiver at the New England 28.
But the Packers' offence stalled when Favre was sacked, putting the Packers back to the 38, and Green Bay later had to settle for a 36-yard Chris Jacke field goal for a 10-0 lead.
The Patriots regained their composure quickly, however, striking back to cut the lead to 10-7 with a 79-yard touchdown drive highlighted by a pair of big pass plays and a pass interference penalty.

Keith Byars caught a one-yard touchdown pass from Bledsoe in the back of the end zone after Green Bay's Craig Newsome was penalised for interfering with New England receiver Shawn Jefferson in the end zone, putting the ball at the one.
During the six-play drive Byars broke a screen pass for 33 yards and Curtis Martin had a 20-yard gain on another screen pass.
The Patriots seized the lead, 14-10, on their next possession when Bledsoe found tight end Ben Coates in the end zone on a four-yard touchdown pass with 2:33 left in the first quarter.
On the previous play -- third-and-one on the Green Bay 48 -- Bledsoe connected with speedy receiver Terry Glenn on a 44-yard pass to the four-yard-line.
The big plays continued early in the second quarter as the Packers regained the lead, 17-14, on the longest touchdown pass in Super Bowl history just 56 seconds into the quarter.

At first down on his own 19-yard-line, Favre found Antonio Freeman streaming down the right sideline for an 81-yard pass play. Freeman raced past safety Lawyer Milloy and Favre delivered the ball right into his hands.
Green Bay increased its lead to 20-14 on a 32-yard Jacke field goal with 8:15 left in the half after an eight-play Packers drive stalled on the New England 13-yard-line.

Green Bay made it 27-14 with 1:11 left in the half when Favre capped a nine-play, 74-yard drive by scrambling for a touchdown from the two, reaching the ball just over the goal line at the front corner before getting knocked out of bounds.
The scoring drive began with a turnover when Bledsoe floated a bad pass into the arms of Green Bay's Mike Pryor, who returned to the 26.
A 22-yard pass over the middle to Freeman and four runs by Dorsey Levens kept the drive moving.
New England got the ball back but was unable to move into scoring position and their drive stalled with 19 seconds left as the Packers took a 27-14 lead into the locker room at intermission.
Green Bay led 35-21 at the end of the third quarter after losing momentum to the Patriots and then grabbing it back in spectacular fashion.

The New England defence came up with big plays in the third quarter to keep Green Bay out of the end zone, including a big stop for a loss of Levens at fourth and one, and a sack of Favre deep in his own territory.
Late in the third, Bledsoe directed an eight-play, 53-yard scoring drive capped by an 18-yard touchdown run up the middle by Curtis Martin to close within 27-21 with 3:27 left in the quarter.
But the euphoria of New England fans was very short-lived.
Howard took the ensuing kickoff at his own 1-yard-line and broke loose, racing 99 yards for the touchdown -- the longest kickoff return in Super Bowl history.
Favre then found Mark Chmura in the back of the end zone for a two-point conversion and the Packers led 35-21 with 3:10 left.
Then it was time for the Green Bay defence to step up and Reggie White sacked Bledsoe on consecutive plays to force a punt from deep in New England territory.
In the fourth quarter, with a 14-point lead Green Bay went into a slowed-down, ball-control mode to try to take time off the clock.
New England, however, was forced to gamble and paid the price when Bledsoe threw his third interception of the game.
On a second and 10 play, Bledsoe tried to go deep to Jefferson, but Craig Newsome picked off the pass to end New England's drive.
Green Bay then held the ball for more than four minutes with a conservative drive, primarily on the ground.
The drive stalled and Jacke missed a 47-yard field goal attempt wide to the right with 3:56 left in the game and the Packers still nursing a 14-point advantage at 35-21.
That proved to be the final score after the Packers picked off yet another pass.
